claims.text: When parsing an HTTPS URL with a non-opaque Unicode hostname, the host is percent-decoded, UTF-8 decoded, and then run through the domain parser using Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing, yielding an ASCII IDNA form such as `xn--53h.example` or `xn--fa-hia.example` rather than raw Unicode in serialized output.

evidence_passages.text: A non-opaque host is parsed by percent-decoding the host, UTF-8 decoding that result, and then running the domain parser. The domain parser uses Unicode IDNA Compatibility Processing, and the standard gives examples such as `☕.example` becoming `xn--53h.example`; its host round-trip table also shows `faß.example` becoming `xn--fa-hia.example`. This means a Unicode hostname in an HTTPS URL is normalized to an ASCII IDNA form, not kept as raw Unicode in the serialized URL. (https://url.spec.whatwg.org/, https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr46/tr46-35.html)

claims.text: For `https`, the default port is `443`; if parsing reads port `443`, the URL record's port is set to `null`, and serialization omits the port.
acceptable_patterns: port is emitted only if it is non-null|serialization omits the port

evidence_passages.text: `https` is a special scheme whose default port is `443`. In `port state`, if the parsed port equals the scheme’s default port, the URL record’s `port` is set to `null`; in serialization, a port is emitted only if it is non-null. So `:443` is normalized away in the parsed URL record and disappears on serialization. (https://url.spec.whatwg.org/)

claims.text: Dot segments are normalized during path parsing: `.` and ASCII-case-insensitive `%2e` are treated as single-dot segments, while `..`, `.%2e`, `%2e.`, and `%2e%2e` trigger path shortening by removing the last path segment.
acceptable_patterns: shorten url'?s path|removes? the last path segment

evidence_passages.text: Dot segments are normalized during path parsing. A single-dot path segment is `.` or an ASCII-case-insensitive match for `%2e`. A double-dot path segment is `..`, `.%2e`, `%2e.`, or `%2e%2e` with ASCII-case-insensitive matching. In `path state`, a double-dot segment triggers “shorten url’s path”, which removes the last path segment; the spec’s note says `/usr/..` becomes `/`. Single-dot segments are omitted from the path, except that the algorithm may append an empty segment when needed at the end. (https://url.spec.whatwg.org/)

claims.text: When the parser encounters `#`, it starts fragment parsing, and fragment code points are UTF-8 percent-encoded using the fragment percent-encode set; because that set includes all code points above `U+007E`, non-ASCII fragment characters are percent-encoded.
acceptable_patterns: sees `?#`|encounters `?#`|starts fragment parsing when it sees `?#`
code points above `?U\+007E`?.+percent-encoded|non-ASCII fragment characters are percent-encoded

evidence_passages.text: The parser starts fragment parsing when it sees `#`. In `fragment state`, each fragment code point is UTF-8 percent-encoded with the fragment percent-encode set. That set includes the C0 control percent-encode set plus space, `"`, `<`, `>`, and `` ` ``; the C0 control percent-encode set includes all code points above `U+007E`, so non-ASCII fragment characters are percent-encoded too. (https://url.spec.whatwg.org/)

claims.text: For path parsing, non-separator path code points are UTF-8 percent-encoded with the path percent-encode set, and the cited parsed-components example shows `%20` remaining percent-encoded in a stored path segment rather than being decoded to a space.

evidence_passages.text: In `path state`, non-separator path code points are UTF-8 percent-encoded with the path percent-encode set. The spec’s parsed-components table shows `file:///ada/Analytical%20Engine/README.md` producing a path segment `Analytical%20Engine`, which is direct evidence that `%20` remains percent-encoded in the stored path segment rather than being decoded to a space. (https://url.spec.whatwg.org/)

claims.text: Parsing lowercases the scheme, so an uppercase HTTPS scheme such as `HTTPS:` becomes `https:`.

evidence_passages.text: Parsing lowercases the scheme: in `scheme start state` and `scheme state`, ASCII letters are appended to the buffer lowercased. For an HTTPS URL, that means `HTTPS:` becomes `https:`. (https://url.spec.whatwg.org/)
